title: MCP Goes Stateless: The 2026-07-28 Specification
content:
## Overview

On July 28, 2026, the Model Context Protocol steering team published the **2026-07-28 specification** — described by the core team as the most substantial rewrite of MCP since its November 2024 launch. The headline change: MCP's transport layer is now **stateless**, removing protocol-level sessions so that any request can be answered by any server instance sitting behind ordinary HTTP load-balancing infrastructure. Six Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs) worked together to get there.

---

## Why Statelessness

Prior MCP versions used a stateful `initialize` / `initialized` handshake tied to an `Mcp-Session-Id` header, pinning a client to a specific server process for the life of a session. That made horizontal scaling awkward — a load balancer had to route every follow-up request back to the same instance. The 2026-07-28 spec removes the handshake and the session header entirely (SEP-2575, SEP-2567), so a stock HTTP load balancer with no sticky sessions can front an MCP server fleet.

---

## What's New

- **Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR, SEP-2322):** Previously, a server needing more input mid-call had to hold a stream open and push a follow-up request down it. Now the server can simply return `resultType: "input_required"` with the questions it needs answered; the client resubmits the original call with an `inputResponses` field attached. This works over plain stateless HTTP, not just long-lived streams.
- **Header-based routing (SEP-2243):** Streamable HTTP requests now carry `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers alongside the JSON-RPC body, so proxies and gateways can route or rate-limit by tool name without parsing the request body.
- **Cacheable list results:** Tool/resource/prompt listings can now be marked cacheable, cutting redundant round-trips for clients that repeatedly enumerate a server's capabilities.
- **Authorization hardening:** OAuth flows were tightened, and **Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) is now formally deprecated** in favor of **CIMD** (Client ID Metadata Documents) — a lighter-weight way for clients to publish identity metadata without a registration round-trip. DCR keeps working for backward compatibility during the transition.
- **Formal extensions framework:** A standardized way for implementations to ship experimental capabilities without forking the core spec.
- **Deprecations:** Roots, Sampling, and Logging capabilities, along with MCP Apps and Tasks, move to deprecated status in this release.

---

## Breaking Changes

This is not a purely additive release. Any server or client relying on the old session handshake, the `Mcp-Session-Id` header, or long-held streams for follow-up questions needs to migrate to the MRTR pattern and the new headers. Tier 1 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, and others) shipped updated betas ahead of the final spec so implementers could test the migration before the July 28 cutover.

---

## Adoption Context

MCP's growth made the rewrite necessary: Tier 1 SDKs were seeing close to half a billion downloads a month by mid-2026, with both the TypeScript and Python SDKs individually passing 1 billion total downloads. At that scale, the stateful session model was becoming a real operational bottleneck for anyone running MCP servers behind standard cloud load balancers — hence the push to a stateless core.

---

## Relevance to Claude Code

Claude Code acts as an MCP client for connectors like GitHub, Slack, and Google Workspace (see the Claude Code Overview page). As MCP servers migrate to 2026-07-28, expect improved reliability when a connector's backing server is scaled across multiple instances, since requests are no longer pinned to the instance that started the session.
